description: A fragmentary order (FRAGO) is an order that changes one or more identified orders. The orders are an operation order (OPORD), an air tasking order (ATO), an airspace control order (ACO) or a special instructions (SPINS) publication. It contains only the changes, as JSON Pointer changes to one identified revision.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

acknowledgement.description: This field gives the acknowledgement instructions.

authentication.description: This field gives the signature block.

base_order.description: This field identifies the base order that this fragmentary order (FRAGO) changes. The reference gives the identifier and the revision, not a file path.

changes.description: This list contains the changes, in order. A consumer makes the changes in the sequence of the list. Validation examines only the structure, and consumers make the changes.

commanders_intent.description: This field gives the changed intent of the commander, as free text.

date_time.description: This field gives the time of signature of the fragmentary order (FRAGO).

effective_time.description: This field gives the time of the start of the effect of the fragmentary order (FRAGO).

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record. The namespace `org.opord-builder.print` contains the data that `opord-builder` puts on each page.

frago_number.description: This field gives the number of the fragmentary order (FRAGO), such as `01`, as free text.

issuing_headquarters.description: This field gives the name of the headquarters that publishes the fragmentary order (FRAGO), as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a fragmentary order (FRAGO).

meta.description: This field gives the identification, revision and issue data of this document.

mission.description: This field gives the changed mission statement, as free text.

references.description: This list contains the documents that the fragmentary order (FRAGO) refers to.

schema_version.description: This field gives the version of the openAIX schema that this document agrees with.

summary.description: This field gives the summary of the fragmentary order (FRAGO), as free text.

time_zone.description: This field gives the letter of the time zone that the order uses for display, such as `Z`. Each time in the document contains an offset.

title: openAIX FRAGO

Acknowledgement.description: An acknowledgement is the instructions for the acknowledgement of the order.

acknowledge.description: The value is `true` when each addressee acknowledges the order.

instructions.description: This field gives the instructions for the acknowledgement, as free text.

Acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement

Authentication.description: An authentication is the signature block of the order.

authenticator_name.description: This field gives the name of the staff officer who authenticates the order, as free text.

authenticator_position.description: This field gives the position of the staff officer who authenticates the order, as free text.

commander_name.description: This field gives the last name of the commander, as free text.

commander_rank.description: This field gives the rank of the commander, as free text.

Authentication.title: Authentication

ChangeTarget.description: A change target is the type, identifier and revision of the order that a change is for.

id.description: This field identifies the order that the change is for. The value is the `meta.id` field of the order.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the order, as one of the enumerated values.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the order that the change is for.

ChangeTarget.title: ChangeTarget

OrderChange.description: A change is one change to an identified order.

op.description: This field gives the operation of the change, as one of the enumerated values.

path.description: This field gives the location of the change, as a JSON Pointer of `RFC 6901`.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the change, as free text.

target.description: This field identifies the order that the change is for.

value.description: This field gives the new value at the location. An `add` or `replace` change shall have this field. A `remove` change shall not have this field.

OrderChange.title: OrderChange

OrderRef.description: An order reference is the identifier and the revision of one order.

id.description: This field identifies the order that this reference is for. The value is the `meta.id` field of the order.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the order. The value is the `meta.revision` field of the order.

OrderRef.title: OrderRef

PrintExtension.description: A print extension is the page data that `opord-builder` puts on each printed page of the order. The namespace is `org.opord-builder.print`, and the group is for this application only.

classification_banner.description: This field gives the classification marking on the top and the bottom of each page.

classification_caveat.description: This field gives the dissemination caveat after the classification marking, such as `REL TO USA, FVEY`, as free text.

copy_number.description: This field gives the number of this copy in the distribution. The number should not be more than `number_of_copies`.

logo.description: This field gives the path or the web address of the logo for the cover page.

message_reference_number.description: This field gives the message reference number that the originator gives to the order, as free text.

number_of_copies.description: This field gives the number of copies in the distribution.

page_icon.description: This field gives the path or the web address of the icon for the header of each page.

place_of_issue.description: This field gives the place where the order is issued, as free text.

watermark.description: This field gives the watermark of each page: short text such as `DRAFT`, or the path or the web address of an image.

PrintExtension.title: PrintExtension

airspace.description: Airspace is a region of airspace with a name, made of volumes that each have a horizontal boundary and vertical limits. The `airspace_type` field gives the class or the type of operation. Shelves, sectors and subtracted volumes use the same structure of components. The control measures for air traffic in Annex B use this contract. Examples are class B airspace, control zones and restricted areas.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

airspace_class_code.description: This field gives the airspace class that the source gives, as one of the enumerated values. When the code is empty, the source gives no class. All classes use the same structure for geometry and altitude.

airspace_type.description: This field gives the class or type of operation of the airspace, such as `ClassB`, `ClassD`, `MTA` or `TMA`, as one of the enumerated values. `MTA` is a military training area, and `TMA` is a terminal control area.

x-enum-descriptions.ADIZ: An air defence identification zone (ADIZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the identification, location and control of aircraft is immediately necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ATCAA: An air traffic control assigned airspace (ATCAA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral limits that air traffic control (ATC) assigns. It separates the stated activities in it from other instrument flight rules (IFR) air traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.ATZ: An aerodrome traffic zone (ATZ) is airspace of defined dimensions around an aerodrome. Its function is the protection of aerodrome traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.Alert: An alert area is airspace that can contain a large quantity of pilot training or an unusual type of flight. This training and these flights are not dangerous to aircraft. Charts show the area to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about it. All flights in it obey the Code of Federal Regulations. Each pilot in it has the same task of collision avoidance.
x-enum-descriptions.CFA: A controlled firing area (CFA) is airspace that contains activities that are a danger to non-participating aircraft when they are not in a controlled environment. They stop at once when spotter aircraft, radar or ground observers find an aircraft that approaches.
x-enum-descriptions.CTA: A control area (CTA) is controlled airspace that extends upwards from a given limit above the surface. Its floor is above the surface, not at the surface. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.CTR: A control zone (CTR) is controlled airspace from the surface to a given upper limit. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassA: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class A airspace is airspace only for instrument flight rules (IFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassB: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class B airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other. In the United States, ATC separates VFR flights with radar. When the radar does not operate, ATC stops this service for VFR flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassC: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class C airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights from all other flights, and VFR flights from IFR flights. VFR flights get traffic information about other VFR flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassD: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class D airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. IFR flights get traffic information about VFR flights, and VFR flights get traffic information about all other flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassE: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class E airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. Only IFR flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary only for IFR flights. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. All flights get traffic information as far as practical. A control zone cannot be class E airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassF: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class F airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. Participating IFR flights get an air traffic advisory service, which separates them from other IFR flights as far as practical. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it. The United States does not use class F airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassG: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class G airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service or separation, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it.
x-enum-descriptions.Danger: A danger area is airspace of defined dimensions in which tasks that are dangerous to the flight of aircraft can occur at stated times. This definition comes from air traffic control.
x-enum-descriptions.FIR: A flight information region (FIR) is airspace of defined dimensions in which flight information service and alerting service are available.
x-enum-descriptions.MOA: A military operations area (MOA) is airspace that is not in class A airspace. It separates flight training of armed forces that is not dangerous from instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft. It also shows visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft where this training occurs. When it is active, air traffic control (ATC) lets an IFR flight go through it only when ATC can separate the flight.
x-enum-descriptions.MTA: A military training area (MTA) is a geographical area that is temporarily or permanently for education and training, which includes exercises and testing. It can include airspace. AJP-3.3.5 gives this area as the training area (TRNG).
x-enum-descriptions.ModeCVeil: A mode C veil is the airspace that is 30 nautical miles or less from an airport in Appendix D, section 1 of 14 CFR part 91. It goes from the surface to 10,000 feet above mean sea level (MSL). Unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes a different procedure, aircraft in it have a serviceable transponder with automatic altitude reporting and serviceable `ADS-B Out` equipment.
x-enum-descriptions.NSA: A national security area (NSA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral dimensions at locations with ground facilities. At these locations, it is necessary to increase security and safety. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) tells pilots to avoid flight through it. A temporary flight restriction (TFR) can temporarily close it to flight.
x-enum-descriptions.Other: The airspace has a local type that is not in this list. The `local_type` field gives the local name of the type.
x-enum-descriptions.Prohibited: A prohibited area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. The state prohibits flight in it.
x-enum-descriptions.RMZ: A radio mandatory zone (RMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of radio equipment is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.ROZ: A restricted operating zone (ROZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates for a given situation or operational need. Examples are refuelling orbits, holding, fires and landing or drop zones. It restricts the operation of one or more airspace users in it.
x-enum-descriptions.Restricted: A restricted area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. In it, the conditions that the state gives restrict the flight of aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.SFRA: A special flight rules area (SFRA) is airspace of defined dimensions, above land areas or territorial waters. In it, the flight of aircraft obeys 14 CFR part 93, unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions.Sector: A control sector is airspace of known horizontal and vertical dimensions. One controller or a group of controllers controls the air traffic in it. The primary traffic flows, the altitude layers and the work of the controllers set its limits. Pilots in it usually speak to air traffic control (ATC) on the frequencies of the sector.
x-enum-descriptions.TFR: A temporary flight restriction (TFR) is a regulatory action of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a notice to air missions (NOTAM). It temporarily restricts some aircraft from operation in a defined area. Its function is the protection of persons or property in the air or on the ground.
x-enum-descriptions.TMA: A terminal control area (TMA) is a control area, usually at the confluence of air traffic services routes near one or more major aerodromes. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.TMZ: A transponder mandatory zone (TMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of a pressure-altitude reporting transponder is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.TRA: A temporary reserved area (TRA) is a defined volume of airspace that one airspace authority usually controls. By common agreement, it is temporarily for another airspace authority. Other air traffic may transit it only with air traffic control (ATC) clearance.
x-enum-descriptions.TRSA: A terminal radar service area (TRSA) is airspace around a designated airport. In it, air traffic control (ATC) gives radar vectoring, sequencing and separation full time. This service is for all instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft and participating visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft. This service is not mandatory for pilots. It is not an airspace class.
x-enum-descriptions.TSA: A temporary segregated area (TSA) is airspace of defined dimensions for the exclusive use of specified users. Their tasks make this necessary. It is for a set period, and no other traffic uses the airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.UIR: An upper flight information region (UIR) is a flight information region (FIR) above a different FIR. Its floor is the ceiling of the lower FIR and is a visual flight rules (VFR) cruising level. Its procedures can be different from the procedures of the lower FIR.
x-enum-descriptions.Warning: A warning area is airspace of known dimensions that starts 3 nautical miles from the coast of the United States. It contains tasks that can be dangerous to non-participating aircraft. Its function is to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about this risk. It can be above the waters of the United States, above international waters or above the two.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace.

components.description: This list contains the airspace volumes of this airspace, in order. Each volume has a floor and a ceiling.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this airspace and its local conditions, as free text.

designator.description: This field gives the designator that a publication or an assignment gives to the airspace. An example is the designator of a restricted area.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airspace. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace.

local_type.description: This field gives the local type name of the airspace when `airspace_type` is `Other`, as free text.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airspace, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace.

state.description: This field gives the State responsible for the airspace, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code such as `DEU`. Under International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 11, paragraph 2.1, this State is responsible for the air traffic services in the airspace. An example is the State of a flight information region (FIR).

type.description: The value identifies this record as an airspace, which is a region made of airspace volumes.

airspace.title: Airspace

airway.description: An airway is an en-route route as a sequence of fixes, with the course, the distance and the altitude limits of each segment.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

airway_type.description: This field gives the class of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.advisory: This value identifies a designated route along which air traffic advisory service is available.
x-enum-descriptions.air_traffic_services: This value identifies a specified route that channels the flow of traffic, as necessary to supply air traffic services.
x-enum-descriptions.airway: This value identifies a control area, or a part of it, in the shape of a corridor. Radio navigation aids identify the corridor.
x-enum-descriptions.area_navigation: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route for aircraft that can do area navigation.
x-enum-descriptions.conditional: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route, or a part of it, that is non-permanent. Aircraft plan and use it only under stated conditions.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this airway.

ident.description: This field identifies this airway as published. An example is `V356`.

level.description: This field gives the altitude structure of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.both: This value identifies the low and the high altitude structures.
x-enum-descriptions.high: This value identifies the high altitude structure.
x-enum-descriptions.low: This value identifies the low altitude structure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airway, for display.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this airway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

segments.description: This list contains the fixes, in airway sequence, in order. Each item has a fix and the segment from that fix to the next fix.

items.description: An airway segment is one airway fix and the segment from this fix to the next fix.

directional_restriction.description: This field gives the direction restriction of the segment, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.backward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in the direction opposite to airway sequence.
x-enum-descriptions.forward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in airway sequence.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from this fix to the next fix, as a length with its unit.

fix.description: This field gives the airway fix at the start of this segment.

inbound_course.description: This field gives the course to this fix from the previous fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

maximum_altitude.description: This field gives the maximum authorized altitude (MAA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the minimum en-route altitude (MEA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

outbound_course.description: This field gives the course from this fix to the next fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure for an airway, with the catalogue code `AIRWAY`. The value selects this contract in a catalogue of control measures.

airway.title: Airway

common.description: Definitions for all openAIX documents are the identifiers, positions, geometry, units, time intervals and resource references that more than one type of document contains.
common.title: openAIX common resources

common.Activation.description: An activation is the time when a control measure is available. It is an interval, a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in an interval, or continuous activation.

continuous.description: The value is `true` when the control measure is active all the time, with no scheduled period in which it is not active.

common.AirspaceComponent.description: An airspace component is one part of an airspace in three dimensions, with a boundary, a floor and a ceiling. Each component adds a volume, subtracts a volume or intersects a volume, in sequence.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this component is available, in the time interval of the parent control measure. This field is optional.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal boundary of this component: points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator. A `geojson` geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.

id.description: This field identifies this component. Each component in its parent airspace has a different identifier.

lower_limit.description: This field gives the floor of this component: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

maximum_limit.description: This field gives the maximum limit of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `upper_limit`, it increases the ceiling. Each value keeps its reference.

minimum_limit.description: This field gives the minimum floor of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `lower_limit`, it replaces the floor. To compare limits with different references, a consumer uses terrain or atmospheric data.

name.description: This field gives the name of this sector or shelf, for display.

operation.description: This field gives the operation of this component on the volume that the components before it make, as one of the enumerated values. The components operate in the sequence of the array, and the first component adds a volume.

upper_limit.description: This field gives the ceiling of this component: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.Altitude.description: An altitude is a vertical position with its unit and its reference: mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

reference.description: This field gives the vertical reference of the altitude, as one of the enumerated values. The value is mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the altitude: feet, metres or flight level, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the altitude, in the unit of `unit`.

common.Altitude.title: Altitude

common.AltitudeBlock.description: An altitude block is a vertical band between a floor and a ceiling. The floor can be the surface, and the ceiling can have no limit.

lower.description: This field gives the floor of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

upper.description: This field gives the ceiling of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.AltitudeBlock.title: AltitudeBlock

common.Bearing.description: A bearing is a direction with its value and its north reference: true north or magnetic north. A magnetic bearing keeps the reference that its author gives. The declination is optional. When the declination is not available, a consumer should show that it cannot change the bearing to true north.

declination_deg.description: This field gives the magnetic declination that changes a bearing from true north to magnetic north, in degrees. This field is optional.

reference.description: This field gives the north reference of the bearing: true north or magnetic north, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the bearing, in degrees from 0 to less than 360.

common.BearingRange.description: A bearing range is a range of bearings from a start bearing clockwise to an end bearing.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the end of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the start of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

common.CasBrief.description: A close air support (CAS) brief is the data that the aircrew get for one CAS attack: the 9-line data of JP 3-09.3 and the mission-level data of the air tasking order (ATO). The ATO and the operation order (OPORD) use this one definition. A field that a use does not need stays out of the record. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Chapter V gives the check-in briefing and the CAS brief.

ato_mission.description: This field identifies the mission of the air tasking order (ATO) that receives the brief. The `orders` field of the operation order (OPORD) identifies the ATO.

check_in.description: This field gives the check-in data for the controller.

contact_points.description: This list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role `control`.

control_type.description: This field gives the type of terminal attack control, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.type_1: This value identifies type 1 terminal attack control, in which the controller sees the target and the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_2: This value identifies type 2 terminal attack control, in which the controller does not see the target or the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_3: This value identifies type 3 terminal attack control, in which the controller gives clearance for all attacks in an area.

controller.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives the brief.

controllers.description: This list contains the agencies and radio channels that control the close air support (CAS) for this brief.

danger_close.description: The value is `true` when the friendly forces are inside the danger-close distance of the weapons for the attack. The value is `false` when the friendly forces are outside that distance.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from the initial point to the target, as a length with its unit.

egress_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the egress point. The point shall have the role `egress`.

final_attack_headings.description: This list contains the ranges of final attack headings that the aircraft can use for the attack. Each range goes clockwise from its start bearing to its end bearing.

fire_support_measures.description: This list identifies the fire support coordination measures that apply to the close air support (CAS) mission.

friendly_direction.description: This field gives the direction from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

friendly_distance.description: This field gives the distance from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as a length with its unit.

friendly_lines.description: This list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.

friendly_marking.description: This field gives the means that marks the position of the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

ground_scheme_summary.description: This field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.

hazards.description: This list contains the hazards in the target area that are not threats.

heading.description: This field gives the heading from the initial point to the target, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.

holding_altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

id.description: This field identifies this close air support (CAS) brief. Each CAS brief in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this CAS brief.

initial_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the initial point of the attack. The point shall have the role `initial`.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the aircraft. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

laser_code.description: This field gives the code of the laser mark, as a laser code with its unit.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this brief.

laser_target_line.description: This field gives the laser target line, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

mark.description: This field gives the type of mark of the target, as one of the enumerated values.

marks.description: This list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.

method_of_attack.description: This field gives the method of attack, as one of the enumerated values.

offset_direction.description: This field gives the side of the line from the initial point to the target on which the aircraft fly the attack, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.left: The aircraft fly the attack to the left of the line from the initial point to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.right: The aircraft fly the attack to the right of the line from the initial point to the target.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

target.description: This field identifies the target of the resource catalogue that the brief is for.

target_description.description: This field gives the target description, as free text.

target_elevation.description: This field gives the elevation of the target, as an elevation with its unit.

target_position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the target, as latitude and longitude.

threats.description: This list identifies the threats of the resource catalogue that are a danger to the aircraft in the target area.

time_on_target.description: This field gives the time at which the weapons hit the target.

time_to_target_seconds.description: This field gives the time from the time of the brief to the time on target, in seconds.

common.CheckIn.description: A close air support (CAS) check-in is the data that the CAS aircrew gives to the controller at check-in. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Figure V-4 gives the check-in briefing.

abort_code.description: This field gives the abort code for the controller and the aircrew, as free text.

items.description: This list contains the parts of the check-in briefing that the aircrew gives.

x-enum-descriptions.abort_code: This value identifies the code that the aircrew uses to make sure that an abort call comes from the controller.
x-enum-descriptions.aircraft_number_and_type: This value identifies the quantity of aircraft in the flight and their aircraft type.
x-enum-descriptions.capabilities: This value identifies the sensors and the other capabilities of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.mission_number: This value identifies the mission number of the flight in the air tasking order (ATO).
x-enum-descriptions.ordnance: This value identifies the weapons on the aircraft, with the quantity of each.
x-enum-descriptions.position_and_altitude: This value identifies the position of the flight at this time, usually from a control point, and its altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.time_on_station: This value identifies the time that the aircraft can stay on station.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the check-in steps.

common.ClassificationLevel.description: A classification level is a security classification of the American government that the banner of an operation order (OPORD) can show.
common.ClassificationLevel.title: ClassificationLevel

common.Coalition.description: A coalition is the side of a record in the simulation: `blue`, `red` or `neutral`. It is simulator data, not real-world data.

common.ControlMeasure.description: A control measure is one openAIX control measure: a reference to one control measure contract, or an extension control measure with a namespace. The `type` field selects the contract.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which the extension control measure is available. The value is a schedule or a flag for continuous activation.

description.description: This field gives the information about this extension control measure and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the extension control measure: a position or a boundary. The geometry uses points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator, or a GeoJSON geometry (RFC 7946).

id.description: This field identifies this extension control measure. Other records and orders use it to refer to this extension control measure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this extension control measure, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this extension control measure, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this extension control measure. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: This field gives the type of the extension control measure, as a name with a namespace.

id.description: This field identifies the control measure of this selection.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure selection. The value is `control_measure`.

common.ControllerContact.description: An agency channel is an agency for the aircrew, with its radio channels.

agency.description: This field identifies the agency or forward air controller that the aircrew speaks to. The value is the identifier of a command and control agency or of a forward air controller (FAC) of the resource catalogue.

alternate_channel.description: This field identifies the alternative radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency when the primary channel is not available.

channel.description: This field identifies the primary radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency.

common.DCSData.description: Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data is the data of a record for DCS. The `bindings` field contains the objects in a DCS mission that are this record or that show it. The other fields contain DCS values that are not objects of a mission.

alic_code.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft launcher interface computer (ALIC) code of the radar. The high-speed anti-radiation missile (HARM) of the DCS F-16C uses this code. Appendix B of the `DCS F-16C Early Access Guide` gives the codes.

angle_deg.description: This field gives the drawing angle from the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission, in degrees. This angle is not a true bearing or a magnetic bearing. Only a consumer with a correct adapter for DCS should use this angle to turn the shape.

beacon.description: This field gives the radio beacon of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object that the record is bound to: the identification, the frequency and the channel as the DCS database gives them. They can differ from the published values of the real station, which the core fields of the record give. The record has at least one of them.

channel.description: This field gives the channel number of the beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, for a beacon that DCS tunes by channel, for example a `TACAN`, an `RSBN` or a landing radio beacon group (PRMG) beacon.

frequency.description: This field gives the frequency of the beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, as a frequency with its unit.

ident.description: This field identifies this beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, as the DCS radio transmits it in Morse code.

bindings.description: This list contains the objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are this record or show it on the map. The record keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of these objects.

clsid.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifier (CLSID) of the load on the pylon. For a rack, the CLSID identifies the rack together with its stores.

clsids.description: This list contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifiers (CLSID) that agree with this store.

coalition.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) coalition of the record: `blue`, `red` or `neutral`, as one of the enumerated values. The coalition is the side of the record in the DCS mission.

label.description: This field gives the label of the pylon in the mission editor.

objects.description: This list contains the units, groups or static objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are parts of the aimpoint.

payload.description: This field identifies the load in the `UnitPayloads` file of the aircraft that agrees with this standard conventional load (SCL).

name.description: This field gives the name of the load in the `UnitPayloads` file.

task_ids.description: This list contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) task numbers of the load. The mission editor shows the load for these tasks, for example `31` for close air support (CAS).

unit_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the aircraft of the load.

projection.description: This field identifies the theatre projection of Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that gives the dimensions and the drawing angle.

pylon.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) pylon number of this station.

settings.description: This field contains the values of the pylon in the mission editor, such as the fuze values. The record keeps them for round trips.

type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the aircraft type, for example `F-16C_50`.

common.DCSObjectRef.description: A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object reference is a link to one object in a DCS mission. The record that contains this reference keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of this identifier.

angle_deg.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) angle of a point or circle drawing, in degrees. The angle is not a true bearing.

closed.description: The value is `true` when the line drawing is a closed shape. The value is `false` when the line drawing is an open line.

group_category.description: This field gives the class of the group: `airplane`, `helicopter`, `vehicle`, `ship` or `train`, as one of the enumerated values.

icon.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) identifier of the icon file.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, as one of the enumerated values. The types are units, groups, static objects, `scenery` objects, airbases, parking stands, drawings and trigger zones.

layer.description: This field gives the drawing layer in the mission editor, such as `Blue` or `Author`.

line_mode.description: This field gives the mode of a line drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.

mission_id.description: This field identifies the mission in which a consumer resolves names and number identifiers. This field is optional.

name.description: This field gives the name of this Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, for display.

native_fields.description: This field contains the attributes from Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that have no typed field. The record keeps them for round trips. A typed field for identifiers, geometry or style shall not go in this object.

object_id.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) number that identifies the object in the mission.

polygon_mode.description: This field gives the mode of a polygon drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.

primitive_type.description: This field gives the drawing primitive in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values. The value is a polygon, a line, a text box or an icon.

style.description: This field contains display attributes from the mission editor, when they are known. The geometry does not change with them.

color.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) colour of the line or text in the format `0xRRGGBBAA`. The format gives the red value, green value, blue value and alpha.

fill_color.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) fill colour in the format `0xRRGGBBAA`. The format gives the red value, green value, blue value and alpha.

font_size.description: This field gives the font size of the text in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS).

thickness.description: This field gives the width of the line in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS).

visible.description: The value is `true` when the drawing shows on the map. The value is `false` when the drawing does not show on the map.

text.description: This field gives the text of a text box drawing, as free text.

unit_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the unit or the static object, when known.

zone_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type of the trigger zone, as one of the enumerated values. The value `circle` is zone type 0, and the value `quad` is zone type 2.

common.DateTime.description: A date-time is an RFC 3339 date-time with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) designator or an offset from UTC, such as `2026-10-02T06:00:00Z`.

common.DocumentRef.description: A document reference is a document that a record refers to. Consumers do not get the document automatically through a network.

id.description: This field identifies the document that the record refers to.

path.description: This field gives the file path of the document.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the document.

section.description: This field gives the part of the document that the record refers to, such as a section or a paragraph.

title.description: This field gives the title of the document.

common.DocumentRef.title: DocumentRef

reference.description: This field gives the vertical reference of the elevation. The value is always `MSL`.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the elevation: feet or metres, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the elevation, in the unit of `unit`.

sim.description: This field contains the simulator data of the record, with the simulator identifier as the key.

common.Frequency.description: A frequency is a radio frequency in kilohertz or megahertz. The modulation is amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM). The modulation and the radio band are optional.

band.description: This field gives the radio band of the frequency, as one of the enumerated values. The band shall agree with the value of the frequency. The limits are 2 to 30 MHz for high frequency (HF), and 30 to 88 MHz for frequency modulation (FM). The limits are 108 to 174 MHz for very high frequency (VHF), and 225 to 400 MHz for ultra high frequency (UHF).

x-enum-descriptions.fm: This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band with frequency modulation (FM) that army radios use, from 30 to 88 MHz.
x-enum-descriptions.hf: This value identifies the high frequency (HF) band, from 3 to 30 MHz, for radio communication at long range.
x-enum-descriptions.uhf: This value identifies the ultra high frequency (UHF) band of the aircraft radios of armed forces, from 225 to 400 MHz.
x-enum-descriptions.vhf: This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band of aircraft radios, from 118 to 137 MHz.

modulation.description: This field gives the modulation of the radio frequency: amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM), as one of the enumerated values. This field is optional.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the frequency: kilohertz or megahertz, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the frequency, in the unit of `unit`.

common.FriendlyMarking.description: A friendly marking is the means that marks the position of the friendly forces for the aircrew.

x-enum-descriptions.chemical_light: This value identifies a chemical light stick that gives light for a short time, usually at night.
x-enum-descriptions.flare: This value identifies a pyrotechnic flare that burns bright at the friendly position.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_strobe: This value identifies an infrared strobe light that aircrew with night vision devices can see.
x-enum-descriptions.mirror: This value identifies a mirror that reflects the light of the sun.
x-enum-descriptions.panel: This value identifies a panel with a bright colour on the ground.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies coloured smoke from a grenade or a canister at the friendly position.
x-enum-descriptions.strobe: This value identifies a visible strobe light that flashes at the friendly position.

common.GeoJSONLineString.description: A GeoJSON line string is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `LineString`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the positions of the line string, in order. Each item is a GeoJSON position.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `LineString`.

common.GeoJSONLinearRing.description: A GeoJSON linear ring is a closed sequence of four or more positions. The first position and the last position shall be the same.

common.GeoJSONMultiPolygon.description: A GeoJSON multipolygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `MultiPolygon`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the polygons of the multipolygon. Each polygon is a list of linear rings, as in a GeoJSON polygon.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `MultiPolygon`.

common.GeoJSONPoint.description: A GeoJSON point is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `Point`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This field gives the GeoJSON position of the point: longitude first, then latitude.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `Point`.

common.GeoJSONPolygon.description: A GeoJSON polygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `Polygon`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the linear rings of the polygon. The first ring is the outer boundary; the other rings are holes.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `Polygon`.

common.GeoJSONPosition.description: A GeoJSON position is a longitude and a latitude in WGS 84 decimal degrees, in this sequence. A third number, the height, is optional. This sequence is the opposite of a geographic point.

common.GeoPoint.description: A geographic point is a position in WGS 84 decimal degrees. An adapter is necessary for the Cartesian coordinates of a simulator.

latitude.description: This field gives the latitude north of the equator, in decimal degrees. A south latitude is a negative value.

longitude.description: This field gives the longitude east of Greenwich, in decimal degrees. A west longitude is a negative value.

common.GeoPoint.title: GeoPoint

common.Geometry_circle.description: A circle geometry is a horizontal disc with a centre and a radius.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the circle, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a circle geometry. The value is `circle`.

radius.description: This field gives the horizontal distance from the centre to the boundary, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_corridor.description: A corridor geometry is a route centreline with a total lateral width.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a corridor geometry. The value is `corridor`.

one_way.description: The value is `true` when aircraft fly the corridor only in the sequence of its points. The value is `false` when aircraft fly the corridor in the two directions.

points.description: This list contains the geographic positions of the centreline, in order. The first position is the start.

width.description: This field gives the total lateral width of the corridor, with the centreline at its centre, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_description.description: A `description` geometry is a text that gives a geographic position or an area, with no coordinates.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a `description` geometry. The value is `description`.

text.description: This field gives the geographic position or area, as free text.

common.Geometry_ellipse.description: An ellipse geometry is an ellipse with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in `extensions.sim.dcs`.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the ellipse, as latitude and longitude.

east_radius_m.description: This field gives the east radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a ellipse geometry. The value is `ellipse`.

north_radius_m.description: This field gives the north radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

common.Geometry_figure_eight.description: A figure-eight geometry is a figure-eight flight pattern with an anchor, an axis, a leg length and a turn radius.

axis.description: This field gives the direction of the axis of the flight pattern from its anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a figure-eight geometry. The value is `figure_eight`.

leg_length.description: This field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.

point.description: This field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the flight pattern, as latitude and longitude.

turn_radius.description: This field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_geojson_line.description: A GeoJSON line geometry is a line as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `LineString` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_geojson_point.description: A GeoJSON point geometry is a point as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `Point` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_geojson_polygon.description: A GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon geometry is a polygon or multipolygon as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_line.description: A line geometry is a sequence of geographic positions that makes an open line.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a line geometry. The value is `line`.

points.description: This list contains the geographic positions of the open line, in order. The first position is the start.

common.Geometry_path.description: A path geometry is an open line of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence. It does not close into an area.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path geometry. The value is `path`.

segments.description: This list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the path. A straight segment that follows a straight segment shall start at its end.

end.description: This field gives the geographic position of the end of the straight segment, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

start.description: This field gives the geographic position of the start of the straight segment, as latitude and longitude.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the arc, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the end of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

radius.description: This field gives the radius of the arc, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the start of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the arc from its start to its end, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `left`, the arc turns to the left side, and with `right`, it turns to the right side.

common.Geometry_point.description: A point geometry is one geographic position.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a point geometry. The value is `point`.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.

common.Geometry_polyarc.description: A polyarc geometry is a horizontal boundary of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a polyarc geometry. The value is `polyarc`.

segments.description: This list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the boundary.

end.description: This field gives the geographic position of the end of the boundary segment, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a boundary segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

start.description: This field gives the geographic position of the start of the boundary segment, as latitude and longitude.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the arc, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the end of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a boundary segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

radius.description: This field gives the radius of the arc, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the start of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the arc from its start to its end, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `left`, the arc turns to the left side, and with `right`, it turns to the right side.

common.Geometry_polygon.description: A polygon geometry is a closed horizontal boundary. The first ring is the external boundary, and the next rings are holes.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a polygon geometry. The value is `polygon`.

rings.description: This list contains the closed rings of positions, in order. The external boundary is first, and the holes come after it.

common.Geometry_racetrack.description: A racetrack geometry is a racetrack with an anchor, an outbound radial, a turn direction and a straight-leg length.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a racetrack geometry. The value is `racetrack`.

leg_length.description: This field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.

point.description: This field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

radial.description: This field gives the outbound bearing from the anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference. The reference is always given: true north or magnetic north. The reciprocal course is the course of the inbound leg.

turn_radius.description: This field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

common.Geometry_rectangle.description: A rectangle geometry is a rectangle with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in `extensions.sim.dcs`.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the rectangle, as latitude and longitude.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

height_m.description: This field gives the height before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a rectangle geometry. The value is `rectangle`.

width_m.description: This field gives the width before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

common.Geometry_sector.description: A sector geometry is a horizontal sector with a centre, a start bearing, an end bearing, and an inner and an outer radius.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the sector, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing of the second side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

inner_radius.description: This field gives the inner radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a sector geometry. The value is `sector`.

outer_radius.description: This field gives the outer radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing of the first side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

common.Geometry_track_racetrack.description: A track racetrack geometry is a racetrack with two end anchors, a lateral width and a turn direction.

a.description: This field gives the geographic position of the first end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

b.description: This field gives the geographic position of the second end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a track racetrack geometry. The value is `track_racetrack`.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

width.description: This field gives the horizontal width of the racetrack, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_vertical.description: A vertical geometry is a coordination level, or the two values of a traverse level. The values of a traverse level are a height above the ground and an altitude above mean sea level.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a vertical geometry. The value is `vertical`.

level.description: This field gives the altitude of the coordination level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the traverse level above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

height.description: This field gives the height of the traverse level above the ground, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a vertical geometry. The value is `vertical`.

common.Hazard.description: A hazard is a danger to the aircraft in the target area that is not a threat.

description.description: This field gives the hazard, as free text.

kind.description: This field gives the type of hazard, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.friendly_aircraft: This value identifies other friendly aircraft in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies friendly artillery, mortar or naval gun fire in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.obstruction: This value identifies an obstruction, such as a tower or a mast.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a hazard that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.terrain: This value identifies high ground in or near the attack run.
x-enum-descriptions.weather: This value identifies a dangerous weather condition in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.wires: This value identifies wires or cables in the air.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the hazard, as latitude and longitude.

common.LaserCode.description: A laser code is a code of four digits for the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of a laser, from `1111` to `1888`. The digits after the first are 1 to 8. Most Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft and weapons accept only codes up to `1788`; the comms standard check warns above it.

common.Length.description: A length is a horizontal distance or dimension with its unit: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the length: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the length, in the unit of `unit`.

common.LinkStation.description: A link 16 station number is a Link 16 station number (STN), which is five octal digits.

author.description: This field gives the name of the author of the document.

classification.description: This field gives the security classification of the document, as one of the enumerated values.

distribution.description: This list contains the addressees that receive the document.

id.description: This field identifies this document. Other records and orders use it to refer to this document.

issued_at.description: This field gives the time of issue of the document.

issuing_unit.description: This field gives the name of the unit that publishes the document.

operation.description: This field gives the name of the operation that the document is for.

references.description: This list contains the documents that this document refers to.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the document.

supersedes.description: This field identifies the document that this document replaces.

title.description: This field gives the title of the document.

common.Offset.description: An offset is a number of minutes from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it. The value can be less than zero.

offset_minutes.description: This field gives the time from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it, in minutes. A negative value is before the start of the period.

common.Offset.title: Offset

common.Period.description: A period is a time interval between two absolute date-times in the RFC 3339 format.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.

common.Period.title: Period

common.PinnedRef.description: A pinned reference is a dependency on a local document that consumers examine by identifier and revision.

id.description: This field identifies the local document of this dependency.

path.description: This field gives the file path of the local document.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the local document. Consumers examine this revision.

common.PinnedRef.title: PinnedRef

common.PointLocation.description: A point location is a geographic point, a location in free text, or the two.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.

position_description.description: This field gives the location, as free text. The text is for a location without accurate coordinates, or it gives more information about the coordinates.

common.Pressure.description: A pressure is an atmospheric pressure with its unit: inches of mercury or hectopascals.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the pressure: inches of mercury or hectopascals, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.inHg: The pressure is in inches of mercury.

value.description: This field gives the value of the pressure, in the unit of `unit`.

activities.description: This list identifies the flight operations that use this radio assignment. Each identifier shall refer to an item of `activities` of the flight. When the list is not given, the assignment is for the complete mission.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that this assignment uses.

preset.description: This field gives the preset number of the radio channel on the radio of the aircraft.

purpose.description: This field gives the operation or objective of this radio assignment, as free text.

radio.description: This field gives the radio of the aircraft that uses the channel, such as `UHF` or `VHF`, as free text.

id.description: This field identifies the external resource catalogue.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the external resource catalogue.

common.RunwayDesignator.description: A runway designator is the magnetic heading of the runway in units of 10 degrees, from `01` to `36`. A suffix can follow: `L`, `R` or `C` for left, right or centre, or `W` for water. Other suffixes are `S` for short take-off and landing (STOL), `G` for glider and `U` for ultralight aircraft.

common.ScheduledWindow.description: A scheduled window is a time interval between two absolute date-times, with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in it.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.

schedule.description: This field gives the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in the interval.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.

common.SimData.description: Simulator data is the data of a record for each simulator, with the simulator identifier as the key, for example `dcs`. The other fields of the record do not change with a simulator. The Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data has fixed fields, and the data of a different simulator is an object with no fixed fields.

dcs.description: This field contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data of the record.

common.Speed.description: A speed is a speed with its unit: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the speed: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the speed, in the unit of `unit`.

common.TACAN.description: A Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) is the channel, band and identifier of a TACAN station.

band.description: This field gives the band of the channel: `X` or `Y`, as one of the enumerated values.

channel.description: This field gives the channel number of the station, from 1 to 126.

common.TACAN.title: TACAN

common.TargetMark.description: A target mark is the means that marks a target for the aircrew. The close air support (CAS) briefs of the air tasking order (ATO) and the operation order (OPORD) use this one list of values.

x-enum-descriptions.illumination: This value identifies a mark from illumination ammunition above or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies a mark from artillery, mortar or naval gun fire.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_pointer: This value identifies a mark from an infrared pointer. Aircrew with night vision devices can see it on the target.
x-enum-descriptions.laser: This value identifies a mark from a laser designator, which the seeker of the weapon or the targeting pod of the aircraft detects.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies a mark from smoke ammunition at or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.talk_on: This value identifies a talk-on, in which the controller tells the aircrew how to find the target by voice.
x-enum-descriptions.tracer: This value identifies a mark from tracer rounds, which show the line of fire to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.white_phosphorus: This value identifies a mark from white phosphorus ammunition at or near the target.

common.VerticalLimit.description: A vertical limit is a floor or a ceiling: an altitude with its reference, the surface, or no limit. The surface is below all altitudes, and the value `unlimited` is above all altitudes.

surface.description: The value is `true` when the limit is the surface. The value is always `true`. The surface is below all altitudes.

unlimited.description: The value is `true` when the limit has no maximum. The value is always `true`. This limit is above all altitudes.

end_day_offset.description: This field gives the day on which the period stops, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `0`, the period stops on its start day, and with `1`, it stops on the next day.

end_time.description: This field gives the time of the end of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as `HH:MM:SS`. The period does not include the end time.

start_time.description: This field gives the time of the start of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as `HH:MM:SS`. The period includes the start time.

weekdays.description: This list contains the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) weekdays on which this period starts.

common.WeeklySchedule.description: A schedule for each week is the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) times in the week when something is available, in the interval that contains it. The intervals in `exclusions` are not part of the schedule.

exclusions.description: This list contains the time intervals with absolute date-times that the schedule subtracts from its periods.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval that the schedule does not include. The value is an absolute date-time.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval that the schedule does not include. The value is an absolute date-time.

periods.description: This list contains the time intervals in each week.

time_reference.description: This field gives the time reference of the schedule. The value is always `UTC`.

common.Window.description: A window is a time interval with limits that are absolute date-times or offsets from the period of the order that contains it.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.

common.Window.title: Window
