ext-kneeboard.description: The `org.opord-builder.kneeboard` extension: kneeboard cards, or overrides of the card built from an ATO flight. On a flight, a card with no `flight_callsign` applies to that flight.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardATCEntry.description: Single ATC / control agency frequency entry.

name.description: Agency name (e.g. 'MARSHAL', 'TOWER', 'DEPARTURE', 'AI CV CONTROLLER').

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCard.description:
A single kneeboard card for DCS World (768×1024 PNG) or print.

Captures the tactical data a pilot needs on the knee: flight lineup,
comms plan, fuel plan, objectives, tanker info, and ATC frequencies.
Values can reference OPORD/FRAGO variables via Jinja2 interpolation.

title.description: Card title / header line (defaults to flight_callsign if blank).

positions.description: Aircraft positions in the flight (lead, wingmen).

timing.description: Package time on target and push.

iff.description: IFF line of the flight: mode 1, mode 4 and mode C. Mode 3 is per position.

weather.description: One line of weather for the mission: clouds, visibility and surface wind of the forecast that covers it.

notes.description: Freeform notes.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCommsPhase.description: Radio assignments for one mission phase.

comm1.description: COMM 1 radio assignment for this phase.

comm2.description: COMM 2 radio assignment for this phase.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCommsPlan.description: Complete communications plan for the kneeboard card.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardPosition.description: Single aircraft position within a flight.

number.description: Position in flight (1 = lead, 2 = wingman, etc.).

mode3.description: IFF mode 3 code of the position (4 digits).

number.description: Steerpoint number: the route point's number, else its position in the route from 1.

name.description: Name of the route point.

altitude.description: Altitude of the route point, with unit and reference.

action.description: Flight phase at the point (ingress, egress, hold, ...).

time.description: Time at the point: the route point's timing (TOT as 1030Z, a window as 1030Z-1045Z), when it has one.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardTACAN.description: TACAN channel plan for the flight.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardTiming.description: Package timing figures for the flight.

ext-measure.title: Measure extension
ext-measure.description: The `org.opord-builder.measure` extension on a control measure: the catalogue code of a measure whose type has none (AXIS, CFZ, SFA, RFZ, SAR, DZ/LZ/PZ, MRR), and the authoring fields of a data-source entry that the typed measure does not carry.

code.description: The control-measure code the authoring model used; only on a measure of type `org.opord-builder.measure`.

extra.description: Authoring field -> value for the fields of the original entry that have no typed home in the measure or that do not read back exactly from it.

ext-order.title: Order extension
ext-order.description: The `org.opord-builder.order` extension: the paragraph content of an order that OpenAIX has no typed field for. It mirrors the paragraphs of the order, and annexes sit under their letter.

theme.description: Name of the document theme to render with (a file in `templates/themes/`, e.g. `wp90`). The `--theme` option wins. Absent for the default look.

document_kind.description: `warno` marks a warning order. Absent for an OPORD.

warno_number.description: Sequence number of the WARNO within the planning effort.

previous_warnos.description: References to earlier WARNOs, so a reader can follow the chain.

previous_fragos.description: References to earlier FRAGOs, so a reader can follow the chain.

base_order_path.description: Path of the base order, relative to this file (FRAGO and WARNO).

resources_path.description: Path of the resources document that `resources_ref` names, relative to this file.

header.description: Leftovers of the order header and task organization.

task_organization_note.description: Short note used in lieu of an inline task organization, typically 'See Annex A (Task Organization).'

references.description: Extra fields of each item, keyed by the identifier of the OpenAIX item; or the whole list when the list has no OpenAIX counterpart.

description.description: Optional human-readable clarification of what the reference is and how it applies to this order.

units.description: Extra fields of each task-organization unit, by unit identifier.

relationship.description: Command or support relationship per FM 3-0: OPCON, TACON, ADCON, assigned, attached, DS, GS, GSR, or R.

ext-order.AARTrack.description:
Named Air-to-Air Refueling track. Tanker assignments to the track are
made in FRAGOs; the OPORD publishes the enduring geometry + radios.

name.description: Track designator (e.g. 'TRACK ARCO', 'TRACK SHELL').

anchor_secondary.description: Secondary anchor (end of track for racetrack tracks).

track_heading.description: Track heading in degrees true (when not defined by two anchors).

tanker_types_supported.description: Airframes that can occupy this track (e.g. 'KC-135R', 'KC-46A', 'KC-130J', 'S-3B').

active_dtg_start.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

active_dtg_end.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

ext-order.AICSector.description:

coverage, assigned to a named controller.

reports_to.description: Parent AWACS callsign this controller reports to.

description.description: Narrative description of the entry.

ext-order.AWACSOrbit.description:

off_station_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

datalink_channel.description: Link-16 channel / MIDS net / DCS datalink ID.

owns_bullseye.description: Bullseye GeoRef name this orbit publishes (matches a GeoRef entry).

ext-order.AirspaceControl.description:

or zones — the OPORD publishes geometry, radios, and controller callsigns

ingress_corridors.description: Extra fields of each item, keyed by the identifier of the OpenAIX item; or the whole list when the list has no OpenAIX counterpart.

ext-order.Appendix.description: A numbered appendix beneath an annex.

number.description: Appendix number within the parent annex (1, 2, 3, ...).

title.description: Appendix title (e.g. 'Intelligence Estimate', 'Target List Worksheet').

body.description: Appendix content. If omitted the appendix is listed in the annex's contents without an inline body.

distribution_list.description: Per-appendix distribution list (recipient organizations), used when this appendix carries a narrower audience than the parent annex.

frequency_tables.description: Radio ladders / frequency plans carried in this appendix. Most commonly used under Annex H, Appendix 1 (Communications Plan).

ext-order.AreaOfOperations.description: Description of the assigned AO with terrain (OAKOC) and weather analysis.

description.description: Narrative description of the AO boundaries and character (rural/urban, restricted/unrestricted, etc.).

terrain.description: OAKOC analysis of the terrain within the AO.

weather.description: Weather analysis and light data for the operation's duration.

ext-order.AssessmentPriority.description: A single assessment priority tied to an objective and phase.

linked_phase.description: Operation phase this priority applies to.

moe_refs.description: MOE identifiers linked to this priority.

mop_refs.description: MOP identifiers linked to this priority.

owner.description: Duty position or staff section owning the priority.

ext-order.AttachmentsDetachments.description: Units attached to or detached from the issuing HQ for this operation.

attachments.description: Units, personnel, or capabilities attached to the issuing headquarters for this operation, with effective DTG if relevant.

detachments.description: Units normally assigned but detached from the issuing headquarters for this operation, with effective DTG if relevant.

note.description: Short note used in lieu of an inline list, typically 'See Annex A (Task Organization).'

ext-order.AttackGuidanceEntry.description: A row of the Attack Guidance Matrix (AGM) per ATP 3-60.

hpt_reference.description: HPT reference (priority rank or descriptor) this row applies to.

when.description: When the HPT is to be engaged relative to acquisition.

restrictions.description: Collateral-damage, ROE, or coordination restrictions on engagement.

ext-order.Authentication.description: OPORD authentication block: acknowledgement, signature, authenticator, and distribution.

acknowledge.description: Whether subordinates must acknowledge receipt of the order; defaults to True per FM 6-0.

commander_last_name.description: Last name of the signing commander as it appears in the signature block.

authenticating_officer_name.description: Name of the officer authenticating the order (typically the XO or S-3) when the commander does not sign personally.

authenticating_officer_position.description: Duty position of the authenticating officer (e.g. 'S-3', 'Executive Officer').

distribution.description: Distribution statement or reference to the distribution annex (typically Annex Z).

ext-order.BCTSTOCellPOC.description: BCT STO cell point-of-contact guidance (UNCLASS level only).

primary_officer_duty_title.description: Duty title of the primary STO officer.

primary_officer_rank.description: Rank of the primary STO officer.

ext-order.BattleRhythmEvent.description: A recurring command-and-staff event on the battle rhythm per ATP 6-0.5.

location.description: Physical or virtual location (CP, VTC room, etc.).

chair.description: Officer or duty position chairing the event.

attendees.description: Required attendees by duty title or staff section.

inputs.description: Required inputs brought to the event (products, estimates, reports).

outputs.description: Products or decisions the event produces.

name.description: Lane designator (e.g. 'RED 1').

entry_grid.description: MGRS grid of the lane entry point.

exit_grid.description: MGRS grid of the lane exit point.

ext-order.BreachOperation.description: A planned breach operation per ATP 3-90.4.

obstacle_description.description: Description of the obstacle being breached (type, composition, density).

alternate_lane.description: Alternate breach lane if the primary fails.

reduction_asset_primary.description: Primary reduction asset (MICLIC, ABV, Bangalore, engineer squad).

marking_standard.description: Lane marking standard (NATO standard or unit SOP).

breach_force.description: Unit designated as the breach force.

breach_dtg_nlt.description: Not-Later-Than DTG the breach must be complete.

ext-order.CAPTrack.description:
Named Combat Air Patrol orbit. FRAGOs assign flights to these by name
(e.g. 'FLY ANCHOR 1') rather than re-publishing the track geometry.

name.description: Track/station designator (e.g. 'ANCHOR 1', 'CAP EAST').

orbit_heading.description: Primary orbit heading in degrees true (for RACETRACK/LINEAR).

orbit_leg_length_nm.description: Leg length in nautical miles (for RACETRACK / FIGURE_EIGHT).

controller_callsign.description: Controlling agency callsign (usually AWACS or AIC, e.g. 'MAGIC').

ext-order.CASRequest.description: A Close Air Support mission request entry.

mission_number.description: CAS mission number issued by the ASOC/ATO.

callsign.description: Flight callsign of the aircraft executing the mission.

ext-order.CCIR.description: Commander's Critical Information Requirements: PIR and FFIR that drive decisions.

pir.description: Priority Intelligence Requirements — information about the enemy, terrain, weather, or civil considerations the commander needs to make a decision.

ffir.description: Friendly Force Information Requirements — information about friendly forces the commander needs to make a decision.

ext-order.CDEGuidance.description:
Collateral Damage Estimation guidance block per CJCSI 3160.01.

Published in Annex D (Fires) so the CDE level referenced on every JPITL,
TST, HPTL, and 9-line CAS entry ties back to a single operation-wide
definition of levels, engagement authorities, weaponeering methodology,
LOAC review authority, and No-Strike / Restricted Target List references.

levels.description: Per-level CDE definitions. Typically all five levels are included with doctrinal text so readers understand each reference.

commanders_guidance.description: Commander's narrative guidance on CDE posture for this operation (e.g. 'favor precision delivery; CDE-3 default for all dynamic targeting').

weaponeering_methodology.description: Weaponeering methodology in use (e.g. 'JMEM', 'Precision Strike Suite (PSS-SOF) v6.1').

loac_review_authority.description: LOAC review authority for target packets at CDE-3 and above (e.g. 'CJTF SJA', 'OSJA').

no_strike_list_reference.description: Current No-Strike List (NSL) version/date in effect for this operation.

restricted_target_list_reference.description: Current Restricted Target List (RTL) version/date in effect for this operation.

documentation_requirements.description: Common documentation expected on every target-approval packet (target folder, imagery, PID evidence, weaponeering worksheet, CDE worksheet, LOAC review memo).

additional_notes.description: Additional CDE-related policy or notes specific to this operation (dynamic-targeting abort authorities, NGO proximity policies, etc.).

ext-order.CDELevelDefinition.description: One row defining a Collateral Damage Estimation level per CJCSI 3160.01.

name.description: Short doctrinal name (e.g. 'Target Validation', 'Casualty Estimation').

description.description: What this CDE step entails and the conditions under which it applies.

engagement_authority.description: Baseline engagement-approval echelon for this level (e.g. 'BN CDR', 'JFLCC', 'CJCS/SECDEF').

documentation_required.description: Documentation required to satisfy this level (imagery, target folder, weaponeering worksheet, LOAC review).

ext-order.COMSECSchedule.description: COMSEC key-load and rollover schedule per ATP 6-02.45.

load_dtg.description: DTG of the initial key load for the operation.

rollover_dtg.description: DTG of the next scheduled key rollover.

controlling_authority.description: COMSEC controlling authority (unit or staff section).

zeroize_triggers.description: Events or conditions that trigger emergency zeroization.

ext-order.COPSource.description: A Common Operating Picture source system per ATP 6-01.1.

ext-order.CallSignEntry.description: A single unit-to-callsign mapping in a signal roster.

unit.description: Unit or element designation (e.g. '2-14 IN', 'VFA-81', 'CJTF-LR Commander').

callsign.description: One or more tactical callsigns for this unit, comma-separated if multiple (e.g. 'HAVOC' or 'SUNDIAL, SOL, INFERNO, LINER').

ext-order.CallSignGroup.description: A categorized group of unit-to-callsign assignments, typically one group per echelon or component.

category.description: Category heading for the group (e.g. 'U.S. Army – 3/10 BCT (10th Mountain Division)', 'Naval Air Wing (CVW-1)', 'Command and Control (C2)').

entries.description: Ordered list of unit-callsign pairs belonging to this category.

ext-order.CivilConsiderations.description: ASCOPE — Areas, Structures, Capabilities, Organizations, People, Events.

areas.description: ASCOPE 'A' — key civilian areas: political boundaries, districts, enclaves, and population centers that affect operations.

structures.description: ASCOPE 'S' — significant structures: bridges, power plants, hospitals, religious sites, and cultural property.

capabilities.description: ASCOPE 'C' — capabilities of the local populace and government to sustain itself (food, water, power, sanitation, security).

organizations.description: ASCOPE 'O' — organizations present in the AO: IGOs, NGOs, religious, tribal, criminal, and political groups.

people.description: ASCOPE 'P' — civilian population: demographics, attitudes, key leaders, and displaced persons.

events.description: ASCOPE 'E' — routine, cyclical, and planned events (elections, religious holidays, market days, harvests) that shape operations.

ext-order.ClassOfSupplyPriority.description: Priority-of-support entry for a single class of supply.

class_of_supply.description: Army class of supply per ADP 4-0 (I=subsistence, II=clothing, III_P=packaged POL, III_B=bulk POL, IV=const., V=ammo, VI=personal demand, VII=major end items, VIII=medical, IX=repair parts, X=non-mil agriculture/econ, WATER=water).

description.description: Short description of what this class covers for this operation.

daily_quantity.description: Planned daily consumption or issue quantity.

source.description: Source of supply (e.g. 'BSB DISTRO CO', 'Theater SSA').

resupply_trigger.description: Trigger that initiates resupply (on-hand threshold, event, or schedule).

ext-order.CollectionRequirement.description: A single collection requirement row per ATP 2-01.

linked_decision_point.description: Linked decision point identifier, if any.

indicator.description: Specific observable indicator to collect against.

collection_asset.description: Asset tasked to collect (unit, platform, or discipline).

ltiov.description: Latest Time Information is Of Value.

reporting_criteria.description: When and how to report observations back to the intelligence cell.

ext-order.Command.description: Paragraph 5.a — Command: location of commander, succession, and command posts.

location_of_commander.description: Location of the commander by phase (e.g. 'With main effort during actions on the objective').

succession_of_command.description: Ordered list of officers who assume command if the commander becomes a casualty.

command_posts.description: Locations and displacement plan for main, tactical, and rear command posts.

ext-order.CommandersIntent.description: Paragraph 3.a — Commander's Intent: purpose, key tasks, and end state per ADP 6-0.

purpose.description: The broader purpose of the operation — the 'why' beyond the mission statement's immediate purpose.

key_tasks.description: Activities the force must perform as a whole to achieve the end state; not specified tasks to subordinates.

end_state.description: The desired conditions at operation's end. Per ADP 5-0, expressed in terms of friendly, enemy, terrain, and civil conditions.

end_state_friendly.description: Desired condition of friendly forces at end state (the 'friendly' category per ADP 5-0).

end_state_enemy.description: Desired condition of enemy forces at end state (the 'enemy' category per ADP 5-0).

end_state_terrain.description: Desired condition of terrain at end state (the 'terrain' category per ADP 5-0).

end_state_civil.description: Desired condition of civil considerations at end state (the 'civil' category per ADP 5-0).

open_door_policy.description: Statement of the commander's open-door policy.

submission_methods.description: Accepted submission methods (in person, form, email, phone, hotline).

acknowledgement_timeline.description: Timeline for acknowledging receipt of a complaint.

confidentiality_and_reprisal_protection.description: Statement of confidentiality and protection from reprisal.

ext-order.ConceptOfOperations.description: Paragraph 3.b — Concept of Operations: how the commander visualizes the operation unfolding.

overview.description: High-level narrative of how the operation will unfold from start to end state.

maneuver.description: Overall maneuver concept tying decisive, shaping, and sustaining operations together.

decisive_operation.description: The operation that directly accomplishes the mission; the main effort at the decisive point per ADP 3-0.

shaping_operations.description: Operations that create and preserve conditions for success of the decisive operation.

sustaining_operations.description: Operations that enable the decisive and shaping operations by generating and maintaining combat power.

reserve.description: Composition, location, priorities, and planned employment of the reserve.

fires.description: High-level concept of fires in support of maneuver; detailed scheme appears in scheme_of_fires and Annex D.

ext-order.Control.description: Paragraph 5.b — Control: command and support relationships and liaison requirements.

command_and_support_relationships.description: Command (OPCON/TACON/assigned/attached) and support (DS/GS/GSR/R) relationships per FM 3-0.

liaison_requirements.description: Liaison officer (LNO) requirements: who sends LNOs to whom, when, and with what capabilities.

ext-order.ControlMeasure.description: A maneuver-graphic control measure: PL, objective, boundary, BP, AA, LD, LOA, DZ/LZ/PZ, NAI/TAI, checkpoint, TRP, etc.

name.description: Control-measure label as it appears on the overlay (e.g. 'PL DAGGER', 'OBJ SWORD', 'CP 21').

type.description: Doctrinal type of the control measure per FM 3-90 / ADP 1-02.

grid_or_trace.description: MGRS grid (point measures) or ordered list of grids defining the trace (linear/area measures).

effective_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

termination_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

purpose.description: Why this control measure exists — the tactical task or synchronization it enables.

ext-order.CoordinatingInstructions.description: Paragraph 3.d — Coordinating Instructions: items applicable to two or more units.

effective_time.description: DTG at which the order becomes effective (often 'On receipt' or a specific DTG).

ccir.description: Commander's Critical Information Requirements (PIR and FFIR).

eefi.description: Essential Elements of Friendly Information — information about friendly forces that must be protected from adversary collection.

fscm.description: Fire Support Coordination Measures (e.g. CFL, FSCL, RFA, NFA) in effect for the operation.

acm.description: Airspace Coordinating Measures (e.g. ROZ, ACA, UA) in effect for the operation.

roe.description: Rules of Engagement applicable to the operation; typically references a SROE/MROE annex or card.

risk_reduction_control_measures.description: Control measures used to mitigate tactical and accidental risks identified in the risk assessment per ATP 5-19.

personnel_recovery.description: Personnel Recovery (PR) guidance: isolated personnel reporting, authentication, and recovery procedures.

environmental_considerations.description: Environmental protection measures and constraints per AR 200-1 that apply to this operation.

themes_and_messages.description: Approved themes and messages that subordinate units reinforce through word and deed.

cema.description: Cyberspace Electromagnetic Activities (CEMA) coordinating instructions per FM 3-12.

time_line.description: Paragraph 3.d Time Line per FM 6-0: sequenced planning and execution milestones (recon LD, confirmation brief, rehearsal, OPORD issue, LD).

earliest_movement_of_forces.description: Earliest DTG at which subordinate units may begin movement; movement may precede full OPORD issue when authorized here.

reconnaissance_and_surveillance_instruct.description: Reconnaissance and surveillance guidance per FM 3-98; typically references Annex L with summary here.

orders_group.description: Commander's orders group meeting — purpose, DTG, location, attendees, products distributed.

rehearsal.description: Rehearsal plan per FM 6-0 Appendix F — type, DTG, location, participants, and method notes.

other.description: Any additional coordinating instructions not captured by the named subfields.

ext-order.CriticalAsset.description: An entry on the Critical Asset List (CAL) per ATP 3-37.2.

category.description: Asset category (personnel, equipment, facility, capability, information).

priority.description: Rank-ordered priority on the CAL (1 = highest).

location.description: MGRS grid location of the asset.

owning_unit.description: Unit owning or operating the asset.

protection_measures.description: Protection measures applied to the asset.

ext-order.CrossAttachment.description: A single cross-attachment or detachment entry used in Annex A.

unit.description: Designation of the attaching/detaching unit (e.g. 'B/2-14 IN').

relationship.description: Command or support relationship per FM 3-0.

direction.description: Whether the unit is flowing IN to this HQ or OUT to another HQ.

parent_or_gaining_unit.description: Parent unit (for attachments IN) or gaining unit (for detachments OUT).

effective_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

termination_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

ext-order.DecisionPoint.description: A Decision Point on the Decision Support Matrix per FM 6-0 App D.

name.description: Short descriptive name for the decision (e.g. 'Commit Reserve').

location_or_nai.description: Physical location (grid) or NAI whose observation triggers the decision.

latest_time_info_of_value.description: LTIOV for the information required to make this decision.

trigger.description: The observable event or condition that forces a decision at this point.

criteria.description: Criteria evaluated when the trigger fires to select the action.

action.description: Action executed when the criteria are met.

alternate_action.description: Alternate action if criteria are not met or conditions change.

linked_ccir.description: CCIR (PIR or FFIR) identifiers whose answers inform this decision.

responsible_staff.description: Staff section or cell responsible for recommending the decision.

phase.description: Operation phase in which this DP is active (1-based).

ext-order.DefendedAsset.description: An entry on the Defended Asset List (DAL) — subset of CAL receiving AMD protection.

priority.description: Rank-ordered priority on the DAL (1 = highest).

location.description: MGRS grid location of the asset.

ext-order.DistributionEntry.description: A single distribution-list entry per FM 6-0 App D.

copy_number.description: Copy number assigned to this recipient.

recipient_unit.description: Unit or organization receiving the copy.

recipient_role.description: Role or duty position of the recipient.

type.description: Action or information addressee.

acknowledgment_required.description: Whether the recipient must acknowledge receipt.

ext-order.EndState.description: Commander's end state broken out into the four ADP 5-0 categories.

friendly.description: Desired condition of friendly forces at end state.

enemy.description: Desired condition of enemy forces at end state.

terrain.description: Desired condition of terrain at end state.

civil.description: Desired condition of civil considerations at end state.

ext-order.EnemyCOA.description: An Enemy Course of Action produced by IPB step 4 per ATP 2-01.3.

designation.description: Standard designator: Most Likely, Most Dangerous, or additional analytic COAs.

title.description: Short descriptive title of the COA (e.g. 'Defend from KUMOR RIDGE').

narrative.description: Narrative of how the enemy is assessed to execute this COA.

indicators.description: Observable indicators that, if seen, suggest the enemy has adopted this COA.

adoption_probability.description: Analyst confidence that the enemy will adopt this COA.

associated_nais.description: NAIs whose observation confirms or denies this COA.

ext-order.EnemyForces.description: Paragraph 1.b — enemy situation: composition, activity, capabilities, and likely/dangerous COAs.

composition_disposition_strength.description: Enemy composition, disposition, and strength (CDS) — who, where, and how many.

recent_activities.description: Summary of recent enemy activity and significant events within the AO and AOI.

capabilities.description: Enemy capabilities and limitations (defend, reinforce, attack, withdraw, delay), often framed by warfighting function.

most_likely_coa.description: Enemy Most Likely Course of Action (ECOA-ML) as produced by IPB step 4.

most_dangerous_coa.description: Enemy Most Dangerous Course of Action (ECOA-MD) as produced by IPB step 4.

ext-order.Execution.description: Paragraph 3 — Execution: intent, concept, schemes by warfighting function, subordinate tasks, and coordinating instructions.

scheme_of_movement_and_maneuver.description: Scheme of movement and maneuver — how forces move and maneuver to accomplish the mission.

scheme_of_mobility_countermobility.description: Scheme of mobility and countermobility — breach, gap crossing, route clearance, and obstacle emplacement.

scheme_of_battlefield_obscuration.description: Scheme of battlefield obscuration — employment of smoke and obscurants in support of maneuver.

scheme_of_reconnaissance_and_security.description: Scheme of reconnaissance and security — R&S operations per FM 3-98 to answer PIR and protect the force.

scheme_of_intelligence.description: Scheme of intelligence — intelligence support to operations; typically references Annex B.

scheme_of_fires.description: Scheme of fires — lethal and nonlethal fires synchronized with maneuver; typically references Annex D.

scheme_of_protection.description: Scheme of protection — protection tasks (AMD, survivability, OPSEC, PR, etc.); typically references Annex E.

stability.description: Stability tasks per ADP 3-07 conducted during or after combat operations to consolidate gains.

scheme_of_engineer_operations.description: Scheme of engineer operations — combat, general, and geospatial engineering; typically references Annex G.

scheme_of_signal.description: Scheme of signal — communications architecture and PACE; typically references Annex H.

scheme_of_information_collection.description: Scheme of information collection — tasking of collection assets to answer CCIR; typically references Annex L.

scheme_of_sustainment.description: Scheme of sustainment — logistics, personnel services, and health services support; typically references Annex F.

scheme_of_cema.description: Scheme of Cyberspace Electromagnetic Activities per FM 3-12; typically an appendix to Annex C.

scheme_of_information_operations.description: Scheme of information operations — integration of information-related capabilities to affect adversary decision making.

scheme_of_airspace_control.description: Scheme of airspace control — airspace management and deconfliction per ATP 3-52.1.

scheme_of_military_deception.description: Scheme of military deception (MILDEC) per FM 3-13.4; usually published under restricted distribution.

scheme_of_space_operations.description: Scheme of space operations — use of space-based capabilities; typically references Annex N.

assessment.description: Assessment plan — MOEs, MOPs, and reporting requirements per ADP 5-0; typically references Annex M.

tasks_to_subordinate_units.description: Extra fields of each item, keyed by the identifier of the OpenAIX item; or the whole list when the list has no OpenAIX counterpart.

coordinating_instructions.description: Paragraph 3.d — instructions applicable to two or more subordinate units.

ext-order.FSCM.description: A Fire Support Coordination Measure per ATP 3-09.32 / JP 3-09.

type.description: FSCM type: Coordinated Fire Line, No Fire Area, Restrictive Fire Area, Restricted Operations Zone, Fire Support Coordination Line, Critical Friendly Zone, No Fire Zone, Airspace Coordination Area, Sensitive Fire Area, Restricted Fire Zone, or Free Fire Area.

name.description: Name or designator of the measure as it appears on the fires overlay.

effective_dtg_end.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

grid_or_coords.description: MGRS grid(s) or ordered coordinates that define the measure's geometry.

establishing_hq.description: Headquarters that established the measure (required when different from the issuing HQ).

remarks.description: Free-text remarks: protected units/assets, special coordination, or exceptions.

ext-order.FrequencyChannel.description: A single channel row in a radio ladder or frequency plan.

name.description: Channel name or net callsign (e.g. 'CASINO', 'CCA TWR', 'BN CMD').

purpose.description: What the channel is used for and which unit or function owns it.

channel_ref.description: Identifier of the channel of the resources document that supplies the name, frequency and purpose of this row. Fields set here replace the channel's.

ext-order.FrequencyTable.description: A radio ladder or frequency plan for a specific platform, site, or band.

title.description: Primary title of the table (e.g. 'UHF (Uniform) Radio', 'Naval Aviation Radio Ladder', 'Battalion Internal Nets').

sub_title.description: Optional scope qualifier (e.g. 'Muwwafaq Salti AB (OJMS)', 'Incirlik AB (LTAG)', 'SINCGARS hopsets').

channels.description: Ordered list of channels in the ladder.

ext-order.FriendlyForces.description: Paragraph 1.c — friendly forces: higher HQ mission/intent, adjacent units, and others that affect this operation.

higher_headquarters.description: Mission and intent of the one-up and two-up higher headquarters.

adjacent_units.description: Missions and tasks of units to the left, right, front, and rear whose actions affect this operation.

other_units.description: Other friendly units (supporting, coordinating, or in adjacent AOs) whose actions affect this operation.

ext-order.GeoRef.description:
Named geographic reference point — bullseye, IP, CP, anchor, waypoint,
NAVAID. Pilots call positions BRAA or bearing/range from these. An OPORD
may publish multiple (primary bullseye + backup + named waypoints).

name.description: Callsign or designator (e.g. 'BULLSEYE', 'IP ALPHA', 'CP DOG').

kind.description: Reference-point category.

coordinates.description: MGRS, L/L, or game-specific coordinate string.

altitude_ft.description: Altitude in feet MSL when applicable (NAVAIDs, elevated fixes).

tacan_channel.description: TACAN channel + band when the reference is a NAVAID (e.g. '73X').

effective_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

notes.description: Freeform notes (e.g. 'Primary bullseye; all BRAA calls reference this point').

ext-order.HNSAgreement.description: A Host-Nation Support agreement per JP 4-08.

name.description: Agreement name or short title.

type.description: Agreement type.

signatories.description: Nations or organizations that signed the agreement.

scope.description: Scope of support provided under the agreement.

nation.description: Host nation the agency belongs to.

ext-order.HVT.description: High-Value Target (or High-Payoff Target when hpt_nomination is True) per ATP 3-60.

priority_rank.description: Rank-ordered priority within the HVT/HPT list (1 = highest).

category.description: Warfighting-function category the target belongs to.

target_description.description: Narrative description of the target: system, unit, facility, or individual.

signature.description: Detectable signature(s) of the target (electronic, thermal, visual, pattern-of-life).

likely_locations.description: MGRS grids or named areas where the target is most likely to appear.

engagement_guidance.description: Commander's guidance for engaging this target (restrictions, priority, delivery).

linked_pir.description: PIR numbers whose answer depends on observing or engaging this target.

hpt_nomination.description: True when the target is nominated to the High-Payoff Target List (HPTL).

medical_command_and_control.description: Medical command and control: medical chain of command, MEDCOM relationships, and supporting medical HQ.

medical_treatment.description: Medical treatment: Role 1–4 care locations, BAS and FSMT positioning, and surgical capability.

medical_evacuation.description: Medical evacuation (MEDEVAC/CASEVAC) plan: MEDEVAC requests, AXPs, dust-off, and ground ambulance routes.

dental_services.description: Dental services: emergency dental care and dental readiness during the operation.

preventive_medicine.description: Preventive medicine: DNBI mitigation, field sanitation, vector control, and water/food surveillance.

combat_operational_stress_control.description: Combat and operational stress control (COSC) per ATP 4-02.8: prevention, triage, and restoration.

veterinary_services.description: Veterinary services: MWD care and food safety/defense inspections.

medical_logistics.description: Medical logistics (MEDLOG) per ATP 4-02.1: CL VIII resupply, blood products, and medical equipment maintenance.

medical_laboratory_services.description: Medical laboratory services supporting diagnostics, health surveillance, and CBRN health threats.

area_medical_support.description: Area medical support: which medical units provide coverage to units without organic medical capability.

ext-order.HigherHeadquarters.description: Mission and intent for two-up and one-up HQ.

two_up_designation.description: Designation of the headquarters two echelons up (e.g. division when this is a battalion order).

two_up_mission.description: Mission statement of the two-up headquarters, quoted verbatim from its order.

two_up_intent.description: Commander's intent of the two-up headquarters, quoted verbatim from its order.

one_up_designation.description: Designation of the immediate higher headquarters (one echelon up).

one_up_mission.description: Mission statement of the one-up headquarters, quoted verbatim from its order.

one_up_intent.description: Commander's intent of the one-up headquarters, quoted verbatim from its order.

ext-order.ISRSyncRow.description: A row of the ISR Synchronization Matrix per ATP 2-01.

time_block.description: Time block covered by this row.

target_or_task.description: Specific target or task within the NAI.

linked_dp.description: Decision point the row supports, if any.

role.description: Role of the asset in this row (primary or alternate).

ltiov.description: Latest Time Information is Of Value for this row.

reporting_method.description: Method used to report observations (net, system, report type).

ext-order.InteragencyPartner.description: An interagency, intergovernmental, or NGO partner per JP 3-08.

coordination_channel.description: Coordination channel used (email, CMOC, LNO, etc.).

bct_hn_lno_required.description: Whether the BCT HN LNO must be involved in coordination with this partner.

ext-order.JPITLEntry.description:
One row on the Joint Prioritized Integrated Target List (JPITL) per JP 3-60 / ATP 3-60.

The JPITL is the JFC-approved, prioritized, integrated target list across
all joint force components. Each row carries approval state, engagement
means, and commander's effect guidance. TST entries live on a separate
list (:class:`TSTEntry`) because their authority and timeline differ.

target_number.description: Target identifier — basic-encyclopedia number (e.g. 'BE-0042-01') or locally assigned 'TGT 0042'.

priority_rank.description: Rank-ordered priority on the JPITL (1 = highest).

target_name.description: Short target name (e.g. 'ENY MRC CP, OBJ HAMMER').

target_description.description: Narrative target description: what the target is and why it matters.

category.description: Warfighting-function category; superset of HVT categories to include joint-level targets.

location.description: Target MGRS grid — point location at time of approval; update on dynamic re-tasking.

component_tasked.description: Joint force component assigned to prosecute this target.

desired_effect.description: Commander's desired effect on the target.

authorized_engagement_means.description: Delivery systems cleared to engage (e.g. 'M777', 'HIMARS', 'F-16 CAS', 'Cyber').

engagement_guidance.description: Commander's intent / restrictions for engaging this target.

cde_level.description: CDE level determined during targeting-approval board.

approval_authority.description: Authority that approved this target (e.g. 'JFC', 'JTCB', 'Component Cdr', 'BN CDR').

status.description: Current lifecycle state.

no_strike_crossref.description: No-Strike List / Restricted Target List entry this target was deconflicted against.

roe_constraints.description: Explicit ROE or LOAC constraints beyond baseline guidance.

review_dtg.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

linked_hvt_rank.description: Optional cross-reference to an HVT/HPTL priority_rank for traceability.

ext-order.KeyLeaderEngagement.description: A planned Key Leader Engagement (KLE) per ATP 3-07.5.

leader_name.description: Name of the leader being engaged.

position.description: Position or role of the leader.

organization.description: Organization or community the leader represents.

engagement_date.description: Planned engagement date (DTG or calendar date).

talking_points.description: Approved talking points for the engagement.

ext-order.KeyMessage.description: An approved key message per FM 3-61.

text.description: The message itself, as approved for release.

priority.description: Message priority within the communication plan.

ext-order.LiaisonElement.description: A liaison element embedded with a partner or host-nation unit.

embedded_with.description: Unit or organization the LNO is embedded with.

rank_required.description: Minimum rank required for the LNO.

language_required.description: Language proficiencies required of the LNO.

ext-order.Logistics.description: Paragraph 4.a — Logistics: the ten logistics functions per ADP 4-0.

sustainment_overlay.description: Reference to the sustainment overlay/graphic depicting LRPs, MSRs/ASRs, and sustainment nodes.

maintenance.description: Maintenance concept: priorities of maintenance, evacuation, and recovery per ATP 4-33.

transportation.description: Transportation concept: MSRs/ASRs, movement control, and mode selection.

supply.description: Supply concept by class (I–X), including CL V basic loads and CL III(B) planning figures.

field_services.description: Field services: shower/laundry, food service, mortuary affairs, aerial delivery, billeting, and water purification.

distribution.description: Distribution concept: throughput, LRPs, convoy operations, and distribution priorities.

contract_support.description: Operational contract support (OCS) per ATP 4-10: contracted capabilities supporting the operation.

general_engineering_support.description: General engineering support to sustainment: base camp construction, horizontal/vertical construction, and real estate.

logpac_interval_hours.description: Interval in hours between successive logistics packages.

first_logpac_dtg.description: DTG of the first scheduled LOGPAC.

link_up_point.description: Named link-up point or grid where LOGPACs meet supported units.

composition.description: Standard LOGPAC composition (trucks, fuel, water, ammo, mail, personnel).

escort_requirement.description: Required escort posture (none, DS platoon, GS section) based on threat assessment.

ext-order.MSRoute.description: A Main Supply Route (MSR) per ATP 4-16.

name.description: MSR designator (e.g. 'MSR IRON').

hazards.description: Known hazards (choke points, known-IED grids, restricted bridges).

controlling_hq.description: Headquarters responsible for movement control on this route.

ext-order.MeasureOfEffectiveness.description: A Measure of Effectiveness (MOE) per ADP 5-0.

statement.description: MOE statement — are we doing the right things?

linked_objective.description: Objective the MOE measures progress toward.

collection_source.description: Source from which data is collected.

threshold.description: Threshold value or condition for assessing effectiveness.

owner.description: Duty position or staff section owning the MOE.

ext-order.MeasureOfPerformance.description: A Measure of Performance (MOP) per ADP 5-0.

indicator.description: Indicator used to measure task performance.

source.description: Source from which performance data is drawn.

owner.description: Duty position or staff section owning the MOP.

ext-order.MediaGroundRule.description: A ground rule governing media engagement.

rule_text.description: The ground rule as written for media.

rationale.description: Doctrinal or operational rationale for the rule.

applies_to.description: Which media category the rule applies to.

ext-order.MinimumRiskRoute.description:
Minimum-Risk Route (MRR) / ingress or egress corridor. Published with
named waypoints that flights follow to avoid friendly fires and SAM rings.

name.description: Route designator (e.g. 'MRR BRAVO', 'INGRESS CORRIDOR 1').

waypoints.description: Ordered waypoints along the route (coordinate strings or GeoRef names).

active_dtg_start.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

active_dtg_end.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

purpose.description: Purpose / use case (e.g. 'Rotary-wing ingress to OBJ HAMMER').

ext-order.NamedAreaOfInterest.description: A Named Area of Interest (NAI) on the intelligence collection overlay.

name.description: NAI designator (e.g. 'NAI 101').

grid_or_boundary.description: MGRS grid (point) or ordered coordinates (line/area) that define the NAI.

linked_dp.description: Decision-point identifier this NAI supports, if any.

activation_dtg.description: DTG the NAI becomes active for collection.

primary_collector.description: Primary collection asset or unit assigned to this NAI.

alternate_collector.description: Alternate collector used if the primary is unavailable.

ext-order.NineLineCAS.description:
9-Line CAS brief — structured tactical brief passed from JTAC/FAC(A)
to CAS aircraft per JP 3-09.3 / AFTTP 3-2.6.

Line order follows doctrinal format: IP → heading → distance → target
elevation → target description → target location → mark → friendlies →
egress. Remarks follow after line 9 (threats, hazards, laser code, TOT,
danger-close ground-commander initials, terminal-control type).

ip_or_bp.description: Initial Point or Battle Position — named reference or coordinates where the aircraft starts the attack run. May reference a published GeoRef (e.g. 'IP ALPHA').

heading_magnetic.description: Magnetic heading from IP/BP to target, in degrees (000-359).

heading_offset.description: Offset side (L or R) when a non-direct attack geometry is required.

distance_nm.description: Distance from IP/BP to target in nautical miles (tenths permitted).

target_description.description: Target type and configuration (e.g. '3x T-72 tanks in hasty defense vic tree line').

target_location.description: Target location — MGRS, L/L, or offset from IP (bearing/distance). Match the format in use for the AO.

mark_type.description: How the target will be marked for the aircraft.

laser_code.description: 4-digit laser PRF code (e.g. '1688') when mark_type is LASER.

friendlies_distance_m.description: Distance from target to nearest friendlies, in METERS.

friendlies_direction.description: Direction from target to friendlies (cardinal or octant, e.g. 'N', 'SW').

friendlies_marking.description: How friendlies are marked (VS-17 panel, IR strobe, chemlight color, smoke, etc.).

egress.description: Egress direction / instructions after weapons release (e.g. 'SOUTH LOW', 'TRACK NORTH TO IP ALPHA').

final_attack_heading.description: Final Attack Heading (FAH) in degrees magnetic, if restricted for deconfliction or terrain.

time_on_target.description: Military date-time group in DDHHMMZMONYY form (e.g. '181200ZAPR26').

time_to_target_min.description: Time To Target (TTT) in minutes from push, if a relative timing is in use instead of TOT.

type_of_control.description: CAS terminal control type per JP 3-09.3 (Type 1/2/3).

cas_callsign.description: CAS flight callsign being briefed (e.g. 'UZI 11 flight of 2 F-16C').

threats.description: Known or suspected threats in the target area (SA-13, ZU-23-2, MANPADS, etc.).

hazards.description: Weather, terrain, or artificial hazards (low ceilings, wires, balloons, restricted airspace).

danger_close.description: True when friendlies are inside danger-close distance for the planned ordnance; requires ground commander initials.

ground_commander_initials.description: Initials of the ground commander authorizing the strike; required when danger_close is True.

remarks.description: Freeform remarks appended to the brief (abort code, restrictions, rules of engagement nuances).

ext-order.OpenAIXRefs.description:
File references to OpenAIX documents that own the air-tasking, airspace and comms facts.

Each value is a file path (relative to this YAML). Once any reference is
set, the OpenAIX files are the single source for those facts and the
inline duplicates (``airspace_control``, ``FrequencyTable``,
``kneeboards[].comms`` and ``kneeboards[].positions``) are rejected.

ato.description: Path to an OpenAIX ATO document (flights, missions, tasking).

aco.description: Path to an OpenAIX ACO document (airspace control measures).

resources.description: Path to an OpenAIX resources document (channels, frequencies, callsigns).

spins.description: Path to an OpenAIX SPINS document (typed SPINS data).

ext-order.OperationPhase.description: A single phase of the operation with start/end conditions and key tasks.

purpose.description: Purpose of the phase — what the force achieves in this phase.

start_condition.description: Condition or event that starts the phase.

end_condition.description: Condition or event that ends the phase and triggers transition to the next phase.

main_effort.description: Designated main effort for the phase.

key_tasks.description: Key tasks the force must accomplish during this phase.

ext-order.OrdersGroup.description:
Commander's orders group meeting per FM 6-0 / ATP 5-0.2-1.

The orders group is the session at which the commander personally issues
the order to subordinate commanders and key staff. Coordinating
Instructions publish purpose, DTG, location, attendees, and products
distributed so subordinates arrive prepared.

purpose.description: Purpose of the orders group (issue OPORD, confirmation brief, back-brief).

location.description: Physical or virtual location (TOC, VTC room, map-brief site).

attendees.description: Required attendees by duty title, subordinate commander, or staff section.

products_distributed.description: Products handed out at the orders group (OPORD, overlays, matrices, keys).

ext-order.PACEPlan.description: A PACE (Primary/Alternate/Contingency/Emergency) plan for a single net.

shift_criteria.description: Criteria that trigger a shift to the next method in the PACE.

ext-order.PIR.description: Priority Intelligence Requirement per ADP 2-0 / ATP 2-01.

number.description: Sequential PIR number within the order (PIR 1, PIR 2, ...).

statement.description: PIR statement phrased as a question the commander needs answered to make a decision.

decision_supported.description: The specific decision (often a decision point) this PIR informs.

nai.description: Named Areas of Interest that will be observed to answer this PIR.

ltiov.description: Latest Time Information is Of Value; after this the answer is no longer useful.

indicators.description: Observable indicators whose presence or absence answers this PIR.

primary_collector.description: Primary collection asset or unit tasked to answer this PIR.

ext-order.PersonnelServices.description: Paragraph 4.b — Personnel Services: HR, finance, legal, religious, and band support.

human_resources_support.description: Human resources support per FM 1-0: PAT, postal, casualty, personnel accountability, and strength reporting.

financial_management.description: Financial management support per FM 1-06: funding, disbursing, and resource management.

legal_support.description: Legal support per FM 1-04: LOAC/ROE advice, claims, military justice, and detainee operations.

religious_support.description: Religious support per FM 1-05: unit ministry team coverage, worship, counseling, and memorial services.

band_support.description: Army band support to ceremonies, morale, and community relations activities.

ext-order.PlanningMilestone.description:
A single planning milestone on a WARNO's parallel-planning timeline.

WARNOs publish these to orient subordinates on recon LDs, confirmation
briefs, rehearsals, OPORD issue, and LD so parallel planning can begin
before the full OPORD is available.

event.description: Short event name (e.g. 'Recon LD', 'Confirmation Brief', 'Combined-Arms Rehearsal', 'OPORD Issue', 'LD').

ext-order.Weather.description:
Paragraph 1.b.(2) Weather — five military aspects, light, forecast, climate, effects.

Per FM 6-0 (May 2022) Appendix D and ATP 2-01.3 Ch 3, the weather
sub-paragraph must cover the five military aspects of weather
(visibility, winds, precipitation, cloud cover, temperature/humidity),
a light table, AND for multi-day operations a forecast keyed to
phases or days — a single snapshot is insufficient for campaign-
scale OPORDs. ``effects_on_operations`` captures the doctrinally
required 'so what' analysis. ``climate_baseline`` provides the
seasonal norm when the forecast confidence is low or the AO is
unfamiliar. The SWO / tactical weather team produces the underlying
Staff Weather Product; this paragraph is the executive summary
with the tables typically living in Annex B (Intelligence).

measure-aca.description: An airspace coordination area (ACA) is a block or corridor of airspace above a target area. In it, friendly aircraft are reasonably safe from friendly surface fires. The airspace control authority establishes a formal airspace coordination area on the request of a component. It has a minimum altitude, a maximum altitude, a baseline, a width on each side of the baseline and effective times. In an informal airspace coordination area, time, lateral distance or altitude keeps aircraft and surface fires apart. A battalion or higher headquarters gives approval for it.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

aca_kind.description: This field gives the type of airspace coordination area (ACA): `formal` or `informal`, as one of the enumerated values. In openAIX, an ACA of the type `formal` is a volume, and an ACA of the type `informal` gives only its method of separation. The airspace control authority makes an ACA of the type `formal` when a component sends a request for it. It has altitudes, a baseline, a width and the times when it is active. In an ACA of the type `informal`, time, lateral distance or altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires. A battalion or a higher unit gives the approval for an ACA of the type `informal`.

measure-area.description: A surface fire support or manoeuvre area is an area on the ground in two dimensions, with no vertical limits. The code `NFA` prevents fires and their effects, and with the code `FFA`, fires can occur without more coordination. With the code `RFA`, fires that do not obey the restrictions of the area can occur only with coordination. The code `EA` identifies the engagement area that the commander plans, and `AOA` identifies the amphibious objective area. The codes `OBJ`, `BP`, `AA`, `NAI` and `TAI` identify ground manoeuvre graphics. The code `FSA` identifies a sea area for fire support ships.

x-enum-descriptions.AA: An assembly area (AA) is an area where a unit makes its preparation for an operation.
x-enum-descriptions.AOA: An amphibious objective area (AOA) is a geographical area that the initiating directive gives for command and control. It contains the objectives that the amphibious task force is to make safe.
x-enum-descriptions.AXIS: An axis of advance is the general area through which the bulk of the combat power of a unit must move. A commander uses it to make the force bypass locations that could delay it. It also shows that the force does not have to clear all of the assigned area. It shows a unit in an encirclement, exploitation or pursuit that it must move quickly toward an objective. Bypass criteria go with it. Any manoeuvre echelon can use one. The axis of a subordinate unit stays inside the axis of its higher headquarters.
x-enum-descriptions.BP: A battle position (BP) is a defence location in the direction of a likely enemy avenue of approach. It is not an area of operations.
x-enum-descriptions.CFZ: A critical friendly zone is an area of friendly weapons locating radar coverage that a commander designates. It is critical to the protection of an asset. The loss of that asset would seriously jeopardize the mission. The zone needs weapons locating radar coverage and attack assets that can give counterfire. The supporting field artillery unit puts enemy indirect fire that the radar acquires into the zone ahead of all other counterfire targets.
x-enum-descriptions.EA: An engagement area (EA) is an area of ground manoeuvre control in which the commander plans to contain and destroy an enemy force. The commander uses the massed effects of all available weapons and the systems that help them. Close air support is an example. The commander may divide the area into smaller areas for subordinate units.
x-enum-descriptions.FFA: A free-fire area (FFA) is a permissive area for fires. Any weapon system may fire into it without further coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). Joint fires can occur more quickly in it, and it helps aircraft jettison munitions. Only the commander with jurisdiction, usually at division or higher, may establish it.
x-enum-descriptions.FSA: A fire support area (FSA) is a sea manoeuvre area that the naval force commander gives to fire support ships. From this area, the ships supply gunfire support to an amphibious operation. The officer in tactical command establishes it.
x-enum-descriptions.NAI: A named area of interest (NAI) is a geospatial area, or a systems node or link, where forces get information for a specified information requirement. This information usually shows enemy and adversary courses of action.
x-enum-descriptions.NFA: A no-fire area (NFA) is a restrictive area that prohibits joint fires and their effects into the area. The establishing headquarters (HQ) may give approval for fires into it, one mission at a time. When an enemy force in the area engages a friendly force, the friendly force may use minimal force in self-defence. A unit of any size may establish an NFA.
x-enum-descriptions.OBJ: An objective (OBJ) is a location for the orientation of operations, the phases of operations, changes of direction and unity of effort. It can be a terrain objective or a force objective.
x-enum-descriptions.RFA: A restrictive fire area (RFA) is an area with special restrictions on joint fires. Units do not fire joint fires that are more than these restrictions, or that have such effects, without coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). A manoeuvre battalion or higher usually establishes it. Restrictive fire areas can also be on-call areas that units prepare before the operation.
x-enum-descriptions.TAI: A target area of interest (TAI) is a geographical area where friendly forces find and engage high-value targets.

measure-fire-support-line.description: A fire support line is one of four lines for the coordination of fires. The headquarters of a ground force, of an amphibious force or of the two forces together sets it. On the far side of a coordinated fire line (CFL), in the boundaries of its headquarters, standard indirect fires can occur without more coordination. Other forces should coordinate their fires on the far side of a fire support coordination line (FSCL) with its commander. A restrictive fire line (RFL) between friendly forces that come together prevents fires and their effects across it without coordination. Between a battlefield coordination line (BCL) and the FSCL, Marine aircraft can attack surface targets without approval from the ground combat element (GCE) commander.

x-enum-descriptions.BCL: A battlefield coordination line (BCL) is a fire support coordination measure of the Marine Corps. Between it and the fire support coordination line (FSCL), Marine air-ground task force (MAGTF) aviation quickly attacks surface targets of opportunity. The approval of the ground combat element (GCE) commander of the area where the targets are is not necessary. The MAGTF commander establishes the BCL. An airspace coordination area (ACA) or a kill box usually includes the area between the BCL and the FSCL.
x-enum-descriptions.CFL: A coordinated fire line (CFL) is a line that a land headquarters sets. Beyond this line, conventional indirect surface fire support means may fire at any time without further coordination. This is applicable only in the boundaries of the establishing headquarters.
x-enum-descriptions.FSCL: A fire support coordination line (FSCL) is a line in the area of operations (AO) for the coordination of fires by other force elements. A land or amphibious force commander establishes it. These fires can have an effect on the current and planned operations of that commander. Other force elements should coordinate these fires with that commander. The establishing commander should coordinate the line with the affected commanders.
x-enum-descriptions.RFL: A restrictive fire line (RFL) is a line between converging friendly forces, of which one or both may move. It prohibits joint fires and the effects of joint fires across the line without coordination with the affected force. Its function is to prevent friendly fire and the duplication of engagements by the converging forces. The commander common to the converging forces establishes it.

measure-isr.description: An identification safety range (ISR) is the minimum range to which aircraft can close to a maritime force without positive identification. This identification shows that the aircraft are friendly. This range makes sure that the maritime force does not mistake the aircraft for hostile. The officer in tactical command sets it. The range moves with the maritime force. A record can give a circle geometry for display at a specified time.

measure-kb.description: A kill box (KB) is a three-dimensional reference system that gives good coordination and control at the correct time, and helps attacks occur quickly. For dynamic targeting operations, it is a permissive fire support coordination measure (FSCM). It decreases the coordination requirements, thus it gives the maximum effects of airpower. Attacks in it occur quickly with less coordination, in the limits of the law of armed conflict (LOAC) and the rules of engagement (ROE). The `killbox_kind` field gives the type, a blue kill box or a purple kill box, from FM 3-09 (2024), paragraph B-19. The firing status `open` or `closed` comes from the assignments in the airspace control order (ACO), not from this record.

coordinating_altitude.description: This field gives the coordinating altitude of the kill box, as an altitude with its unit and reference. A blue kill box can start at this altitude, not at the surface. The source is the multi-service procedures for the kill box (2009).

A blue kill box lets aircraft attack surface targets, and it starts at the surface or at its coordinating altitude. A purple kill box also lets surface units fire at surface targets, and it has an altitude floor.

x-enum-descriptions.blue: Air-to-surface attacks in the kill box occur with no further coordination with the area of operations (AO) commander. The kill box extends from the surface to a ceiling altitude. Units coordinate indirect fires that hit in it or go through it. The coordination is with the airspace control element, the kill box coordinator or the aircrew on station.
x-enum-descriptions.purple: Air-to-surface attacks, surface-to-surface fires and subsurface-to-surface fires in the kill box occur with no further coordination with the area of operations (AO) commander. The kill box has an altitude floor, and aircraft do not fly below the floor. Indirect fires that stay below the floor need no further coordination.

measure-line.description: A coordination line is a line on the ground, with points in sequence, for the coordination of manoeuvre or identification. The line is the forward line of own troops (FLOT), the forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) or a ground manoeuvre graphic. These graphics are the phase line, the boundary, the limit of advance (LOA), the line of departure (LD) and the line of contact (LC). Other lines show where friendly aircraft set their identification, friend or foe (IFF) equipment to off or on.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

x-enum-descriptions.left: The enemy is on the left side of the line, from its first point to its last point.
x-enum-descriptions.right: The enemy is on the right side of the line, from its first point to its last point.

x-enum-descriptions.BOUNDARY: A boundary is a line that delineates surface areas for the coordination and deconfliction of operations. These operations are between units, formations or areas that are next to each other.
x-enum-descriptions.FEBA: A forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) is the foremost limits of the areas of the ground combat units. It does not include the areas of the covering or screening forces. It helps to coordinate fire support, the positions of forces and manoeuvre.
x-enum-descriptions.FLOT: A forward line of own troops (FLOT) is a line that shows the most forward positions of friendly forces at a given time. This is applicable to any kind of military operation.
x-enum-descriptions.IFFOFF: An identification, friend or foe switch-off line (IFFOFF) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft stop the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft stop their IFF transponder at this line, before they go to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.IFFON: An identification, friend or foe switch-on line (IFFON) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft start the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft start their IFF transponder again at this line, after the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.LC: A line of contact (LC) is a general trace that delineates the location where friendly and enemy forces engage each other. In the defence, it is frequently the same as the forward line of own troops (FLOT). In an offensive operation, it can be the same as the line of departure (LD).
x-enum-descriptions.LD: A line of departure (LD) is a line in land warfare that coordinates the departure of attack elements.
x-enum-descriptions.LOA: A limit of advance (LOA) is a phase line that controls the forward progress of the attack. The attack unit does not advance its elements or assets across this line. The unit may move its security forces up to the line.
x-enum-descriptions.PL: A phase line (PL) is an identifiable feature in the operational area, for the control and coordination of military operations. A phase line is not a boundary, unless the commander designates it as a boundary.

measure-mez.description: A missile engagement zone (MEZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in air and missile defence, normally reserved for engagements by surface-to-air missile (SAM) weapon systems. It is an air defence measure. In maritime zone coordination, it is together with the fighter engagement zone (FEZ) and the joint engagement zone (JEZ). Its limits are a sector, an altitude, a range and bearing from a point of origin, or a mixture of these. Aircraft should coordinate before they go into it. The `mez_kind` field gives the type of zone from JP 3-01 (2012), V-11.

The value is a high-altitude missile engagement zone (HIMEZ), a low- to medium-altitude missile engagement zone (LOMEZ) or a short-range air defence engagement zone (SHORADEZ). Each of the catalogue codes `HIMEZ`, `LOMEZ` and `SHORADEZ` agrees with one of these values.

x-enum-descriptions.high: This value identifies a high-altitude missile engagement zone (HIMEZ), in which high-altitude surface-to-air missiles usually engage the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.low: This value identifies a low- to medium-altitude missile engagement zone (LOMEZ), in which surface-to-air missiles for low and moderate altitudes usually engage the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.short_range: This value identifies a short-range air defence engagement zone (SHORADEZ), in which short-range air defence (SHORAD) weapons usually engage the aircraft.

measure-misarc.description: A missile arc (MISARC) is an area of 10 degrees in maritime operations, or larger when the officer in tactical command gives that order. Its centre is on the bearing of the target, and its range extends to the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile (SAM). The arc has its centre on the firing unit, and its axis is the bearing of the target. Its width is 10 degrees by default, and its range is the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile.

measure-route.description: An air route or corridor is a centreline with points in sequence and with vertical limits. Corridor codes also have a lateral width. Only a published visual flight rules (VFR) route (`VFRRTE`) can have no vertical limits. The type code gives the task of the route, and it tells if the route has air traffic services. It also gives the area that the route is for: a rear area, a forward area, a maritime force or a base defence zone. Aircraft can fly a corridor in the two directions, but not when its geometry has the `one_way` flag.

x-enum-descriptions.AIRCOR: An air corridor (AIRCOR) is a restricted air route of travel for friendly aircraft. Its function is to prevent friendly forces from firing on friendly aircraft. Its altitudes are not more than the coordinating altitude, when there is one.
x-enum-descriptions.AIRRTE: An air route (AIRRTE) is the navigable airspace between two points, with only the identification that is necessary to apply flight rules. It is a bi-directional route. It can go through air defences as a minimum-risk route. Only support traffic uses it.
x-enum-descriptions.APPCOR: An approach corridor (APPCOR) is airspace for the safe passage of land-based aircraft that join a maritime force or go from it. The corridor usually goes from an entry and exit gate to the centre of the force. Its inner boundary is the identification safety range (ISR).
x-enum-descriptions.LLTR: A low-level transit route (LLTR) is a temporary low-level corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area. It decreases the risk to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces.
x-enum-descriptions.MRR: A minimum-risk route (MRR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions that the ground commander recommends for aircraft. It has the minimum known hazards to low-flying aircraft that transit the combat zone. Aircraft usually use it to cross the forward line of own troops (FLOT). It is usually not near close air support (CAS) target areas.
x-enum-descriptions.SAAFR: A slow aviation assets flight route (SAAFR) is a route below the coordination level for land component aviation assets in the forward area. The route is for their movement in direct support of ground operations.
x-enum-descriptions.SC: A special corridor (SC) is an air corridor for the special routing requirements of some missions in air operations.
x-enum-descriptions.SL: A safe lane (SL) is a bi-directional lane from an airbase, a landing site or a base defence zone (BDZ) to adjacent routes or corridors. It can connect more than one of them. Safe lanes can also connect adjacent activated routes or corridors.
x-enum-descriptions.TC: A transit corridor (TC) is a bi-directional corridor in the rear area that routes aircraft through friendly air defences with minimum risk. Air traffic services are not normally available in it.
x-enum-descriptions.TMRR: A temporary minimum-risk route (TMRR) is a temporary minimum-risk route for air traffic. It goes between transit routes, or the rear boundary of the forward area, and its operations area. The route is for direct support of ground operations.
x-enum-descriptions.TR: A transit route (TR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area for air operations. It decreases the risks to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces. It is a bi-directional route, and it should avoid weapons free zones and base defence zones.
x-enum-descriptions.VFRRTE: A published visual flight rules route (VFRRTE) is a route on a chart for visual flight rules (VFR) flights around, under or through complex airspace, such as class B airspace. A VFR flyway is a general flight path, not a specific course, and it needs no air traffic control (ATC) clearance. A VFR corridor goes through class B airspace with defined vertical and lateral limits, and it needs no ATC clearance. A VFR transition route is a specific flight course on a chart. On it, communication with ATC is necessary, and an ATC clearance is necessary in class B airspace.

items.description: A route vertex is a vertex of the route geometry with its name or its point record.

index.description: This field gives the position of the vertex in the route geometry, from 0 at the start. The vertices of a path are the start of each segment and the end of the last segment. The index shall be smaller than the number of vertices, and the indexes shall increase in the list.

name.description: This field gives the name of this route vertex, for display. An example is the charted name of a visual reporting point.

point.description: This field identifies the point record that is at this vertex.

It gives the defenders one more procedure to identify friendly aircraft. The record gives the level as a height above the ground and as an altitude above mean sea level.

measure-volume.description: An airspace coordination volume is an airspace with a name and given dimensions, made of components in sequence. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling. The type is a code from North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) AJP-3.3.5 Annex B or from doctrine. The code gives the task of the volume and the airspace users that can or cannot go in it. The agency that controls the volume does the coordination of entry and operations.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace coordination volume is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace coordination volume.

components.description: This list contains the airspace components of the volume, in order. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace coordination volume.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace coordination volume has an effect on.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace coordination volume, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace coordination volume, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace coordination volume. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
